title: Oncall playback and handoff review - Aug 05 2026
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a structured playback of the on-call activity for the week of 2026-07-27 -> 2026-08-02, focused on the intermittent tokenization service degradation (see linked Slack thread). It is intended for the on-call rotation, triage owners, and the follow-up action owners. This is a working draft — final postmortem will be a separate confluence doc after action items are complete.

Summary / TL;DR:
- Incident: intermittent 503s from tokenization microservice leading to increased request latencies and ~3.5% elevated error rate for hosted-api customers between 2026-07-30 02:10 UTC and 2026-07-30 05:50 UTC (multiple short spikes).
- Impact: customer requests surfaced increased latencies and occasional 5xxs, some retry storms on client side. No data leakage, no control-plane compromise.
- Root cause (hypothesis): a combination of a regressed memory leak in tokenizer cache eviction + an autoscaler misconfig for the tokenizer deployment. Under certain request patterns, pods hit memory pressure, OOM-kill cycles, and kubelet restarts leading to transient 503s while new pods torn up.
- Immediate mitigation: temporarily pinned tokenizer image to previous stable tag, scaled replica count to absorb load, and bumped node pool ephemeral memory thresholds.
- Next steps: follow-up tasks to harden cache eviction, improve autoscaling policy, add richer SLO-based alerting, and implement a circuit-breaker at the API gateway to reduce retry amplification.

Timeline (playback, UTC):
- 2026-07-30 02:08 — Pager fired: elevated 5xxs on hosted-api region-us-east-1. Pager duty alert: hosted-api-5xx-rate > 0.8% for 5m. On-call: Miguel T. acknowledged at 02:09.
- 02:12 — Initial triage: observed error spikes correlated to tokenization service returning 502/503. No obvious network partition.
- 02:22 — Quick mitigation: routed small fraction (~15%) of traffic to fallback tokenization cluster in region-us-west-2 (manual routing rule) to reduce pressure while investigating.
- 02:28 — Logs show repeated GC pauses and OOM kill events in tokenizer pods. Memory usage showing steady climb after a recent rollout (image tag: tokenizer:v2026-07-28-b3).
- 02:35 — Attempted to roll back tokenizer to v2026-07-22-stable in canary; immediate improvement in that canary.
- 02:47 — Some worker nodes reached kubelet eviction pressure; new pods entering CrashLoopBackOff. Autoscaler didn't bring up nodes fast enough due to min-cpu/memory guardrails.
- 03:05 — Mitigation: increased tokenizer replicas from 3 -> 6 and manually increased node pool memory headroom.
- 03:40 — Observed reduction in 5xx rate to baseline ~0.2%. Fallback routing gradually removed.
- 05:10 — Post-mitigation monitoring showed stable baselines but intermittent bump at 05:43 when a spike reappeared after a client synthetic load test. Reopened investigation; found a slightly different traffic pattern exposing the same leak.
- 05:50 — Decide to pin tokenizer image to stable for all regions and schedule a maintenance window for deeper rollback + fix. On-call handoff prepared for follow-up tomorrow.

Metrics / SLO snapshot during event:
- SLO affected: hosted-api availability (5xx rate) target = 99.9% per rolling 30d.
- During window (02:10-05:50): availability dropped to ~99.45% for the affected region for that window (short-term blip; rolling 30d impact minimal but customer visible).
- Mean P95 latency rose from baseline 150ms -> 420ms at spike peaks.
- Tokenizer pod memory: baseline 1.1 Gi -> observed 2.9 Gi before OOM.

Initial root-cause analysis (working hypothesis):
- Regression introduced in tokenizer service around commit 3a7f4b2: a change to the in-memory prefix-cache eviction logic caused rare retention of large tokenization buffers. Under a particular mix of long-context requests, buffers were retained and not freed promptly, leading to memory growth.
- Autoscaler configuration (HPA + cluster-autoscaler) had conservative thresholds and a cooldown that prevented quick scale-up under bursty pressure. Together these caused cascading pod restarts and transient 503s.

Immediate actions taken (already done):
- Rolled back tokenizer to v2026-07-22-stable in all regions (Anika R.).
- Increased tokenizer replicas and node pool memory headroom (Liam O'C.).
- Created temporary routing rule to fallback cluster to limit customer impact (Priya D.).
- Added short-term dashboard widgets for tokenization memory per-pod and OOM events (Miguel T.).

Recommended follow-ups (action items):
- SRE-1011: Add deterministic unit/integration tests for tokenizer cache eviction behavior; owner: Priya Desai; due: 2026-08-12; linked: JIRA-SRE-1011.
- SRE-1012: Harden autoscaler policies: reduce cooldown, add step-scaling rules for high memory pressure, and validate node pool limits; owner: Liam O'Connell; due: 2026-08-10; linked: JIRA-SRE-1012.
- SRE-1013: Implement circuit-breaker on gateway for tokenization errors to throttle client retries and prevent amplification; owner: Anika Rao; due: 2026-08-19; linked: JIRA-SRE-1013.
- SRE-1014: Run chaos test that simulates tokenizer memory leak + autoscaler lag to validate mitigations; owner: Miguel Torres; due: 2026-08-15; linked: JIRA-SRE-1014.
- SRE-1015: Postmortem write-up and customer-communication draft for affected customers; owner: Product Incident Lead (TBD); due: 2026-08-09; linked: CONFLUENCE-POSTMORTEM-2026-07-30.

On-call handoff notes (for next rotation):
- Current state: tokenizer pinned to v2026-07-22-stable globally. Replica count is 6 in us-east-1, 4 in other regions. Node pool headroom increased.
- Monitoring: keep an eye on tokenization.memory_per_pod, tokenization.oom_count, hosted_api.5xx_rate (1m/5m), and gateway.retry_backoff.
- Pager thresholds adjusted temporarily: hosted-api-5xx-rate -> warn at 0.5%, page at 0.8% (was 0.8%/1.2% previously). This is temporary until autoscaling rules updated.
- Handoff checklist completed: rollback confirmed, routing rules removed except fallback standby, dashboards updated, incident Slack channel archived with summary.

Retro notes / learnings:
- Deploy fast + validate: the risky change landed without sufficient memory regression tests. We need low-friction pre-merge tests for memory heavy services.
- Autoscaling is only as good as its thresholds: cooldowns and step rules must reflect the service memory profile, not just CPU.
- Circuit-breakers upstream would have greatly reduced customer-visible retries.
- Observability gaps: tokenization memory metrics were coarse-grained; pod-level allocation metrics should be standard for memory-sensitive services.

Meeting agenda for follow-up (2026-08-06 16:00 UTC, SRE meeting room):
- 10m: Recap and playback owner updates.
- 20m: Dev deep-dive on tokenizer cache code and proposed change set for SRE-1011.
- 15m: Autoscaler configuration review and rollout plan for SRE-1012.
- 10m: Gateway circuit-breaker design review (SRE-1013).
- 5m: Next steps and owners confirmation.

Appendix: quick checklist for on-call responders (copied to rotation handbook)
- Acknowledge pager within 5m and set the incident channel.
- Quick triage: determine if error is localized to a microservice by checking 3-dot view (gateway -> tokenizer -> downstream).
- If memory pressure suspected: check pod memory timeline, recent deploys, GC logs. Consider immediate rollback to last-known-good.
- If node pool pressure: raise node pool headroom; consider manual scale if autoscaler lagging.
- If retries amplifying: implement temporary routing/fallback and raise gateway throttle.

Notes to self / unresolved questions:
- Need to validate if there is any client behavior that increases buffer retention unexpectedly (long-running streams or a specific customer traffic shape). Product to reach out to top 5 impacted customers to collect request patterns.
- Determine whether tokenizer library upgrade (two months ago) contributed; codeowner trace requested.

If you are reading this as the next on-call: please review action items above, poke at the linked artifacts, and add yourself as owner in Jira where relevant. We'll convert this to the final postmortem after the fix and tests land.

-- Anika R., oncall lead (week of 2026-07-27)
